questions.question: When driving a bobtail tractor, what should you know?

options.text: Bobtails cannot drive as fast as tractors with semitrailers.
Bobtails take longer to stop than tractors with semitrailers.
Bobtails are illegal in most states.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bobtails take longer to stop than tractors with semitrailers.
questions.explanation: A bobtail tractor has no semitrailer attached. When driving a bobtail, it takes longer to stop than when driving a tractor with a loaded semitrailer.

questions.question: If oil and water build up in your air tanks, your brakes:
questions.correctAnswerText: May not work correctly.
questions.explanation: Drain air tanks daily to remove water and oil. Too much oil and water in the air tanks can damage your brakes.

questions.question: If you drive a vehicle made before 1998 and are not sure if the trailer has Anti-Lock Brakes (ABS), you can:

options.text: Look for wheel speed sensors behind the brakes.
Look for a red light on the front right corner of the converter dolly.
Pump the air brakes to activate the ABS.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for wheel speed sensors behind the brakes.
questions.explanation: Check under the trailer for wheel speed sensors behind the brakes to see if the trailer has ABS.

questions.question: What does a tractor protection valve do?

options.text: It keeps air in the tractor brakes if the trailer breaks away or leaks.

questions.correctAnswerText: It keeps air in the tractor brakes if the trailer breaks away or leaks.
questions.explanation: A tractor protection valve keeps air in the tractor brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a bad leak.

questions.question: Using the trailer hand valve while driving:
questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause a skid.
questions.explanation: Never use the trailer hand valve while driving. It can cause your trailer to skid.

questions.question: What is another name for the service line?
questions.correctAnswerText: Control line
questions.explanation: The service line is also called the control line. It carries air to the trailer brakes and is controlled by the foot brake or trailer hand brake.

questions.question: Which type of vehicle is most likely to have a "crack-the-whip" effect?

options.text: A five-axle tractor with one semitrailer
A three-axle tractor with one semitrailer

questions.correctAnswerText: A triple trailer
questions.explanation: Triple trailers are most at risk for the "crack-the-whip" effect.

questions.question: When backing a trailer, which direction should you turn the steering wheel?

options.text: Turn the wheel toward the direction you want the trailer to go.
Turn the wheel away from the direction you want the trailer to go.
It depends on where you are backing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the wheel away from the direction you want the trailer to go.
questions.explanation: When backing with a trailer, turn the wheel away from where you want to go. Once the trailer starts turning, switch the wheel direction to follow the trailer.

questions.question: Why is proper coupling technique important?

options.text: It is the same on all vehicles.
It is essential for safe vehicle operation.
It means the fifth wheel plate should not be greased.
It can be learned over time.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is essential for safe vehicle operation.
questions.explanation: Proper coupling and uncoupling is critical for safe operation of combination vehicles. Bad coupling is dangerous.

questions.question: Simply changing lanes can cause:

options.text: A "crack-the-whip" effect that can cause a rollover.
Confusion about which lane the driver wants to use.

questions.correctAnswerText: A "crack-the-whip" effect that can cause a rollover.
questions.explanation: Changing lanes too quickly in a combination vehicle can cause a "crack-the-whip" effect and result in a rollover.

questions.question: What is true about fully-loaded rigs?

options.text: They are less likely to roll over than empty rigs.
They are more likely to roll over than empty rigs.
They are just as likely to roll over as empty rigs.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are more likely to roll over than empty rigs.
questions.explanation: Fully-loaded rigs have a higher center of gravity because of the cargo weight. They are 10 times more likely to roll over in a crash than empty rigs.

questions.question: When are rollovers most likely to happen?
questions.correctAnswerText: When drivers turn too fast.
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when a driver turns too fast. You should slow down before entering turns and curves, especially when pulling a fully-loaded rig.

questions.question: When should an air supply control lever be in its normal position?

options.text: When applying the trailer emergency brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: When pulling a trailer.
questions.explanation: In older vehicles, tractor protection controls may have levers instead of knobs. When an air supply control is in its normal position, it is properly set for pulling a trailer.

questions.question: If you cannot back your trailer in a straight line, what should you do?

options.text: Swerve back and forth while backing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Back toward the driver's side.
questions.explanation: If you cannot back your trailer in a straight line, back on a curved path toward the driver's side. This gives you the best view while backing.

questions.question: When traveling below 40 mph, how much following distance should you keep for every 10 feet of your vehicle?
questions.correctAnswerText: One second
questions.explanation: At speeds below 40 mph, allow at least one second of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle. At faster speeds, use the same formula but add one extra second. Larger vehicles need more space to stop.

questions.question: How many air lines does a combination vehicle have?
questions.correctAnswerText: Two air lines.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles have two air lines: a service line and an emergency line.

questions.question: How should the trailer hand valve be used for parking?

options.text: It should always be used for parking.
It should only be used for parking on a downhill.
It should never be used for parking.
It should only be used when transporting cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: It should never be used for parking.
questions.explanation: Do not use the trailer hand valve for parking. It can cause air to leak out of the brake system, which releases the brakes. Use the parking brake instead.

questions.question: What happens when a trailer's wheels lock up?

options.text: The trailer will usually continue to move in a straight line.
The trailer will likely swing around.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer will likely swing around.
questions.explanation: When a trailer's wheels lock up, the trailer tends to swing around. This can cause a trailer jackknife.

questions.question: What height should a trailer be when connecting a converter dolly to a second or third trailer?

options.text: Slightly higher than the center of the fifth wheel.
Level with the center of the fifth wheel.
Slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel.
Next to the center of the fifth wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel.
questions.explanation: When connecting a converter dolly to a second or third trailer, the trailer should be slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel.

questions.question: Before backing your tractor under the trailer, the trailer brakes should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Locked.
questions.explanation: Before backing your tractor under the trailer while coupling, make sure your trailer brakes are locked. This is an important step for safely coupling and uncoupling a combination vehicle.
